"Evaluate exactly.

$$
\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} 2 \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

Choose the exact value."] [:db/add "fa64c59d-5f3f-5931-be67-99fe5fe1efaf" :question/worked-solution "Let $u=2 x$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=2.
$$

Transform both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\pi}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=\pi\\x=\frac{3 \pi}{4}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{3 \pi}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{3 \pi}{4}} 2 \cos{\left(2 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\int_{\pi}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}} \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=\sin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Endpoint values: $\sin{\left(\pi \right)}=0,\quad \sin{\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2} \right)}=-1$.

Integrate and evaluate:

$$
\left[\sin{\left(u \right)}\right]_{\pi}^{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}=\left(-1\right)-\left(0\right).
$$

The answer is

$$
-1.
$$"] [:db/add "fa64c59d-5f3f-5931-be67-99fe5fe1efaf" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "fa64c59d-5f3f-5931-be67-99fe5fe1efaf" :question/answer-fields $$

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\pi}{2}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{3 \pi}{2}\\x=\frac{2 \pi}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=2 \pi\end{aligned}
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\frac{2 \pi}{3}} \sin{\left(3 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi} \sin{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \sin{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=- \cos{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Endpoint values: $\cos{\left(\frac{3 \pi}{2} \right)}=0,\quad \cos{\left(2 \pi \right)}=1$.

Integrate and evaluate:

$$
\left[- \frac{\cos{\left(u \right)}}{3}\right]_{\frac{3 \pi}{2}}^{2 \pi}=\left(- \frac{1}{3}\right)-\left(0\right).
$$

The answer is

$$
- \frac{1}{3}.

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int \sin{\left(3 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int \sin{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}

$$
\int \sin{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=- \cos{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \cos{\left(3 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}

$$
\int \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=\sin{\left(u \right)}+C.

$$
\left[\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)}}{3}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}=\left(0\right)-\left(\frac{1}{3}\right).
$$

$$
- \frac{1}{3}.

$$

Transform both bounds:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\pi}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{2}\\x=\frac{\pi}{3}&\Longrightarrow u=\pi\end{aligned}
$$

Including the differential factor gives

$$
\begin{aligned}&\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{3}} \cos{\left(3 x \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x\\&=\frac{1}{3}\left(\int_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi} \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).\end{aligned}
$$

Use the integration rule:

$$
\int \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u=\sin{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Endpoint values: $\sin{\left(\frac{\pi}{2} \right)}=1,\quad \sin{\left(\pi \right)}=0$.

Integrate and evaluate:

$$
\left[\frac{\sin{\left(u \right)}}{3}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{2}}^{\pi}=\left(0\right)-\left(\frac{1}{3}\right).
$$

The answer is

$$
- \frac{1}{3}.
$$"] [:db/add "66ade998-4eef-53a7-accd-bf6073145230" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy] [:db/add "66ade998-4eef-53a7-accd-bf6073145230" :question/answer-fields
